theorem: For every PPT nonnegative diagonal weighted operator R on the 2024 Krebs–Gachechiladze 5x5 grid generators in frontier-20261028-grid55-weighted-coordinate-theorem-v1.json SHA256 f1e892255a20d6c3b23afa42994a5fe90feea3be1cb63979a135e6da3ea702c6, deleting ANY one computational basis row on Alice produces a 4x5 PPT operator with SN<=2; deleting ANY one computational basis column on Bob produces a 5x4 PPT operator with SN<=2. Consequently arbitrary further local maps on the opposite subsystem cannot yield Schmidt number3. In particular, every 4x4 output for which at least one rank-four local map has a coordinate kernel line has SN<=2, even when the opposite kernel is arbitrary complex. The unprojected PPT assumption is essential to the proof, and no global 4x4 claim is made.
source_and_ppt_minors: The source is https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12966v1 Figure 2, with A=|02>+|11>+|20>, V=|01>, W=|10>, B=|12>+|34>, C=|21>+|43>, Q=|22>+|33>, and loops |00>,|14>,|23>,|32>,|41>. Let alpha,beta,delta,b,c be the nonnegative weights of A,V,W,B,C. Because R is PPT, the PT principal matrices on |01>,|12> and on |10>,|21> respectively imply beta*b>=alpha^2 and delta*c>=alpha^2. If alpha=0, the original defining sum already has SR<=2.
alice_coordinate_deletions: If Alice row0,1,or2 is removed, A itself reduces to SR<=2 and the defining nonnegative sum works. If row3 is removed, B reduces to |12>, V remains |01>, and A remains SR3. When alpha>0, beta>0 and beta*b>=alpha^2; with z^4=1, q_z=sqrt(alpha)*A'+z*sqrt(beta)|01>+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(beta))|12> has the first two head rows proportional and is SR<=2. Its phase average consumes alpha[A']+beta[01]+alpha^2/beta[12], leaving b-alpha^2/beta>=0 and other SR2 terms. If row4 is removed, C reduces to |21> while W remains |10>, and q_z=sqrt(alpha)*A'+z*sqrt(delta)|10>+conjugate(z)*(alpha/sqrt(delta))|21> has the last two head rows proportional. The remaining coefficient c-alpha^2/delta is nonnegative. These identities hold on the full 4x5 output, not just after an additional Bob cut.
bob_coordinate_deletions: Swapping the tensor factors preserves positivity, PPT and Schmidt number; it sends A to A, swaps V with W, swaps B with C, fixes Q and |00>, and exchanges the loop pairs (14,41) and (23,32). Hence it permutes the weighted source family even when individual weights are unequal. The Alice proof applied to the swapped source gives the Bob assertion. Explicitly Bob column3 reduces C to |21> and uses W; Bob column4 reduces B to |12> and uses V. Bob columns0,1,2 reduce A to SR<=2.
arbitrary_other_map: A local linear map sends every SR<=2 ket to a ket of rank<=2 and preserves a nonnegative decomposition. Therefore, once any one-side cut is SR2, any subsequent local map on the opposite side preserves SN<=2. A surjective rank-four map with a specified coordinate kernel equals an invertible output map composed with the associated coordinate deletion, so the conclusion includes all such maps and arbitrary opposite rank-four kernels. PPT is preserved by all local maps.

exact_check.observed: For the explicit trace24 PPT/SN3 weighted source pinned in the cited predecessor, the checker hash-pins and replays the 25-cut weighted check, then checks all ten 4x5/5x4 source cuts. It verifies all 400 entries of each actual decomposition, 16 phase vectors by every 3x3 minor, and nonnegative PT pivots for all ten cuts. All checks passed. The arbitrary complex opposite maps and arbitrary weights follow from the written local-map and phase identities, not from finite examples.

limits: The source must be PPT and in the specified nonnegative diagonal grid family, and at least one local kernel must be a coordinate line. Both non-coordinate 5x5 kernels, generic 4x4 PPT states, an SN>=3 witness, novelty and external/formal review remain open.
